introduction.text: Casal Rotondo is a Roman mausoleum on the Appian Way, southeast of Rome, near the sixth mile of the ancient road. Built around 30 BC, it is a circular tomb about 27 metres across, topped by a later farmhouse that gave the monument its name. The site was also used as a lookout along the road. Beside the tomb, a brick wall assembled by archaeologist Luigi Canina displays an inscription and sculptural fragments found nearby. The inscription led to a proposed identification of the tomb's owner, but that connection is disputed.

history.description: Built around 30 BC near the sixth mile of the Appian Way, the mausoleum belonged to a stretch of road lined with tombs.
The farmhouse built above the ancient remains gave Casal Rotondo its name. The site was also used as a lookout along the Appian Way.

design.description: The ancient tomb is circular, with a diameter of about 27 metres. The later farmhouse stands on top of its surviving structure.

Archaeologist Luigi Canina assembled the nearby display of fragments. An inscription naming Cotta once suggested a connection to the family of Messalla Corvinus. That interpretation is disputed: the fragment is thought to come from a smaller neighbouring tomb.
